text:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: release v1.4.3 -> us-west canary (3 pods). CI: https://ci.redwood.example/build/8912 :rocket:

alice: seeing errors on canary health checks, 502s and 500s. digging in logs now.

carla: paging oncall, errors look KMS-related in app logs: 
```
ERROR 2026-03-15T21:02:11Z Service=ingest: Failed to decrypt SECRET_DB_KEY: PermissionDenied: Request had insufficient authentication scopes.
```

incident-bot: @oncall-sre triggered page (PD-INC-7523) — severity: SEV2 — response expected within 15m :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: i'm on it. linking logs and deployment info. can anyone confirm which SA the canary pods use?

ben: canary uses infra-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com (same SA used in previous canaries). I see a new KMS key rotation run at 20:55 UTC in the audit logs.

alice: stacktrace shows 403 from KMS: "permission denied for cryptoKeyVersions.decrypt" — might be IAM binding removed during rotation.

carla: quick check: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/prod-secret-key` returns binding list, i'm getting no binding for infra-runner SA.

dion: omg that explains canary failures. 3 pods failed decrypt, readiness probes failed -> 502s. impact is limited to canary pool only so far.

eve-support: any customer-facing impact? should we start a support banner?

alice: preliminary metrics: canary traffic only (~1% of traffic, specific hostpool us-west-canary). error rate on that pool ~38% for the last 6m. production stable otherwise. no major customer 500 spikes seen on primary.

oncall-sre: action plan: 1) disable canary routing (kill-switch feature flag) 2) rollback canary deployment 3) re-add IAM binding for infra-runner SA 4) redeploy canary / validate. doing step 1 now.

ben: how do we toggle the kill-switch?

noncall-sre: using Console -> Routing -> canary_weight = 0, or via internal API: `POST /routing/traffic` payload `{ "canary_weight": 0 }` — doing it now.

deploy-bot: Canary traffic set to 0% by noncall-sre (was 1%).

carla: doing rollback: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/ingest --to-revision=12` on us-west-canary cluster. pods terminating.

alice: rollback complete, all canary pods replaced with previous revision. health checks green. error rate on canary hostpool dropping to 0 within 60s.

incident-bot: PD incident updated: status = acknowledged. responders: oncall-sre, alice, carla, ben.

ben: I'll re-add the IAM binding. recommended role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter (or kafka-safe equivalent). running: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/prod-secret-key --member=serviceAccount:infra-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`

carla: careful — recent rotation created a new key version and the rotation job intentionally removed a legacy binding. need to confirm we restore correct princips per rotation runbook.

ben: added binding. `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` now shows infra-runner with decrypter role.

alice: redeploy canary? or do we run a smoke job first?

noncall-sre: run smoke test first. I'll re-enable routing to 0% still, re-deploy a single canary pod with latest revision and run decrypt tests.

dion: spinning one canary pod, logs show `Decrypt success` on startup now ✅

carla: smoke passed. rolling canary to 1% again and monitoring metrics.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout resumed: canary_weight=1%.

alice: after re-enable, canary metrics stable, no decrypt errors. rolling out to wider pool will follow normal cadence.

eve-support: Support note: impact limited to canary traffic; ~3 customers briefly saw degraded responses. No outage to general customers. craft short message: "We briefly paused a canary deploy due to a configuration issue with key permissions; no broader impact. Investigating root cause and will follow up."

dion: assigning follow-ups: - audit KMS rotation automation (carla) - add pre-deploy KMS permission check to release CI (alice) - improve runbook steps for rotation rollback (ben) - postmortem + RCA doc (oncall-sre).

carla: quick note — rotation job had a concurrent IAM cleanup change that removed service account binding when creating new key version. Ops change slipped review. adding rollback guard.

noncall-sre: lifting page. closing PD after we verify no regression for 30m. handoff: i'll summarize in postmortem and hand to SRE for RCA.

oncall-sre: short timeline to include in postmortem: 20:55 rotation job, 20:58 deploy started, 21:02 decrypt errors observed, 21:04 kill-switch and rollback executed, 21:12 IAM binding restored, 21:18 canary smoke passed, 21:24 canary resumed.

incident-bot: Incident PD-INC-7523 marked RESOLVED pending postmortem doc.

eve-support: thanks all — i'll prepare the customer update and coordinate with comms for a follow up tomorrow.

oncall-sre: postmortem owners: oncall-sre (lead), carla (rotation automation), alice (CI checks). target: publish within 72h.

ben: quick wins pushed to backlog: - add pre-deploy KMS IAM check (CI fail if missing) - require rotation job to not remove bindings needed by runtime SA until new key verified - add monitoring alert for KMS decrypt 5xx spikes per hostpool.

alice: adding CI check PR now: link https://git.redwood.example/p/alice/check-kms-iam/pulls/7

carla: opened rotation change PR for safer cleanup and manual approval gate: https://git.redwood.example/p/ops/rotation/pulls/42

oncall-sre: thanks team. closing thread once postmortem link is up. good incident containment. :party_popper:
